    "chunk_summary": "Introduction of a finance-domain paper defining information fidelity as a decision-centered criterion for LLM context compression, naming decontextualization and model dependency as fidelity-loss patterns, and proposing agentic context compression."
  },
  "concepts": [
    {
      "id": "c_information_fidelity",
      "name": "information fidelity",
      "aliases": ["decision-centered fidelity criterion"],
      "description": "A decision-centered criterion under which a compressed representation preserves the decision implied by the original source.",
      "anchor": "evaluate information fidelity",
      "location": "1 Introduction"
    },
    {
      "id": "c_context_compression",
      "name": "Context compression",
      "aliases": ["LLM context compression"],
      "description": "Compressing a long source document into a shorter context passed on to another model or a human decision-maker.",
      "anchor": "Context compression can cause",
      "location": "1 Introduction"
    },
    {
      "id": "c_long_context_compression",
      "name": "Long-context compression",
      "aliases": ["long-document compression"],
      "description": "Compression of long source texts, described as inherently open-ended because no single correct summary exists.",
      "anchor": "Long-context compression",
      "location": "1 Introduction"
    },
    {
      "id": "c_decontextualization",
      "name": "Decontextualization",
      "aliases": ["context stripping"],
      "description": "A fidelity-loss pattern in which headline claims are preserved while decision-relevant caveats, comparisons, or expectation framing are stripped away.",
      "anchor": "Decontextualization",
      "location": "1 Introduction"
    },
    {
      "id": "c_model_dependency",
      "name": "Model dependency",
      "aliases": ["compressor dependency"],
      "description": "A fidelity-loss pattern in which which evidence survives compression varies systematically across compressor models.",
      "anchor": "Model dependency",
      "location": "1 Introduction"
    },
    {
      "id": "c_agentic_context_compression",
      "name": "agentic context compression",
      "aliases": ["source-grounded compression"],
      "description": "A procedure in which an agent generates competing compressed contexts and audits their disagreements against the original source.",
      "anchor": "as agentic context compression",
      "location": "1 Introduction"
    },
    {
      "id": "c_compression_induced_decision_flip",
      "name": "Compression-induced decision flip",
      "aliases": ["decision flip", "compression-induced decision flips"],
      "description": "A decision-maker reaching a different decision from the one supported by the original source after compression.",
      "anchor": "Compression-induced decision flip",
      "location": "1 Introduction"
    },
    {
      "id": "c_llm",
      "name": "Large language models",
      "aliases": ["LLMs"],
      "description": "Models increasingly used to compress long documents into shorter contexts before those contexts are passed to another model or a human decision-maker.",
      "anchor": "Large language models",
      "location": "1 Introduction"
    }
  ],
  "definitions": [
    {
      "id": "d_information_fidelity",
      "term": "information fidelity",

    }
  ],
  "claims": [
    {
      "id": "cl_failure_mode",
      "claim_text": "an LLM-compressed representation can lead a decision-maker to make a financial judgment that differs from the judgment supported by the full source text",
      "claim_type": "empirical",
      "evidence_grade": "inference",
      "anchor": "consequential failure mode",
      "location": "1 Introduction"
    },
    {
      "id": "cl_evals_gap",

      "claim_type": "empirical",
      "evidence_grade": "inference",
      "anchor": "do not directly test",
      "location": "1 Introduction"
    },
    {
      "id": "cl_headline_facts",
      "claim_text": "A summary may retain headline facts but omit the caveats or offsets needed to interpret them, remaining factually correct while inducing a different decision",
      "claim_type": "speculative",
      "evidence_grade": "inference",
      "anchor": "may retain",
      "location": "1 Introduction"
    },
    {
      "id": "cl_strip_caveats",

      "claim_type": "speculative",
      "evidence_grade": "inference",
      "anchor": "stripping away",
      "location": "1 Introduction"
    },
    {
      "id": "cl_context_removed",
      "claim_text": "When such context is removed, a factually correct summary can still carry a different decision implication",
      "claim_type": "speculative",
      "evidence_grade": "inference",
      "anchor": "When such context is removed",
      "location": "1 Introduction"
    },
    {
      "id": "cl_analyses_vary",
      "claim_text": "investment analyses vary across LLMs",
      "claim_type": "empirical",
      "evidence_grade": "inference",
      "anchor": "investment analyses vary",
      "location": "1 Introduction"
    },
    {
      "id": "cl_not_random",
      "claim_text": "decision change is not merely random degradation",
      "claim_type": "empirical",
      "evidence_grade": "inference",
      "anchor": "merely random",
      "location": "1 Introduction"
    },
    {

    }
